zh.summary: 依政策分開管理資訊揭露、資料權限與傳輸保護，以允許及拒絕測試保留正當服務。

sourceBody.text: 這一課其實是在教你一個非常重要的資安觀念：
資安不是讓所有人都無法取得資料，而是讓正確的人，在正確的條件下，只能取得他應該取得的資料。
例如，公司有一台伺服器，裡面有員工名單、財務資料、設備資訊。
我們希望達成三件事：

items: 財務人員可以正常使用財務資料。
一般員工可以使用自己工作需要的資料，但不能讀取機密文件。
外部陌生人不能任意探查公司的內部系統。

sourceBody.text: 但這裡有個陷阱：如果你直接把整台伺服器關閉，大家確實都無法列舉資訊了，卻也無法正常工作。
因此，真正的目標是 安全性與可用性同時成立。
一、先搞懂：列舉到底有什麼危險？
Enumeration（列舉）就是向系統詢問：「你這裡有哪些東西？」
想像你走進一間公司，詢問櫃檯：
「你們有哪些部門？員工有誰？財務室在哪裡？有哪些電腦？資料櫃放在哪裡？」
這些問題看起來沒有直接偷走任何資料，但如果陌生人能拿到完整的內部清單，就比較容易找出值得進一步攻擊的目標。
不過，列舉並不等於入侵。許多正常業務也需要查詢資訊。

visual.caption: 圖 1｜同一個 Finance 資料夾，可能有三種不同的結果
visual.description: 三個平行能力，沒有先後箭頭；名稱可見不表示可讀，能讀也不表示能改。

items.title: 看得到名稱
items.body: 知道 Finance 存在

items.title: 讀得到內容
items.body: 可以開啟財務報表

items.title: 改得了內容
items.body: 可以修改財務報表

sourceBody.text: 這三個權限完全不一樣。
有人看得到資料夾名稱，不代表能讀取文件；能讀取文件，也不代表能修改文件。
這就是列舉防護的第一個重點：資訊揭露、資料讀取、資料修改，要分別管理。
二、資安防護的四個關卡
我們把伺服器想成一間有保全的大樓。

visual.caption: 圖 2｜一個使用者想讀取伺服器資料
visual.description: 箭頭表示依序檢查四個問題。這是理解用的示意圖；實際協定不一定依這四步執行，傳輸保護也可能在登入前建立。

items.title: 第一關：網路可達性
items.body:
防火牆讓不讓你連到這個服務？

像大樓外面的圍牆和入口。

items.title: 第二關：身分驗證 Authentication
items.body:
系統能不能確認你是誰？

像櫃檯核對員工證件。

items.title: 第三關：存取授權 Authorization
items.body:
就算你是員工，你能看哪些文件、做哪些操作？

像確認你有沒有財務室的鑰匙。

items.title: 第四項：傳輸保護 Encryption / Integrity
items.body:
資料在傳送途中有沒有被偷看或竄改？

像用上鎖、防拆封的公事包運送文件。

sourceBody.text: 特別注意兩個初學者經常混淆的問題。
問題 A：我已經登入了，為什麼還不能讀取資料？
因為 Authentication（確認身分）不等於 Authorization（給予權限）。
例如，你確實是公司的員工，但是你不是財務部門成員，因此不能讀取財務報表。
問題 B：我已經啟用 HTTPS 或 TLS，資料是不是就安全了？
不是。
TLS 能保護傳輸過程，也能在正確驗證憑證的條件下協助確認伺服器身分，但如果系統本身允許一般員工讀取機密資料，那麼 TLS 只是把「不該給的資料」安全地送到錯誤的人手上。
三、什麼是最小權限（Least Privilege）？
一句話：
你完成工作需要多少權限，我就只給你多少，不多給。
例如公司聘請一位清潔人員。
他需要進入走廊、會議室、洗手間，但不需要董事長的保險箱密碼。
在資訊系統也是一樣。
例如 SNMP 監控帳號，需要知道路由器目前的流量和介面狀態，卻不需要修改路由器設定。
如果管理員為了方便，直接給這個監控帳號最高權限，雖然監控程式可以正常工作，但帳號一旦外洩，就可能產生更嚴重的風險。
所以資安人員不只要問「功能能不能用」，還要問「是不是給了超出需求的權限」。
四、前面學過的協定，應該如何防護？
把 M04 前面所有列舉課程整合起來，防護思路其實一致：限制不必要的資訊，但保留正當服務。

rows: 正常名稱查詢可用，但區域資料傳送 AXFR 應限制給核准對象
依身分限制檔案的讀取、修改與刪除
控制哪些人能查哪些帳號與欄位
限制來源、安全層級及可讀寫的管理物件
控制登入、列目錄、下載與上傳
限制不必要的使用者驗證與名單查詢線索
可以正常校時，但限制不必要的管理資訊查詢
系統間通訊及舊式名稱服務
盤點相依關係後，限制不需要的入口及資訊揭露

sourceBody.text: 其中有兩個很適合 CEH 考試理解的例子。
例子一：SNMPv3 是不是就一定安全？
不一定。
假設你把 SNMP 換成 v3，而且使用 `authPriv`，這代表在適當設定下，訊息具備認證、完整性及加密保護。
但如果同一個帳號仍然被授權讀取所有敏感設備資訊，問題仍然存在。
你還需要透過 VACM 等存取控制設定，限制它真正能讀取或修改的管理物件。
記住：
`authPriv` 主要處理通訊安全；`read view / write view` 主要處理操作權限。
例子二：SMB 有簽章，就等於加密嗎？
不等於。
你可以把它想成寄送文件。

items: Signing（簽章）：像具有驗證能力的封條，協助確認訊息未遭未授權竄改。
Encryption（加密）：像將文件放入上鎖的箱子，避免途中被旁觀者讀取。
Access Control（存取控制）：決定收件人到底有沒有資格拿到文件。

sourceBody.text: 這三者不能互相取代。

技術依據：[SNMPv3 訊息安全 RFC 3414](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3414.html)、[VACM RFC 3415](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3415.html)、[Microsoft SMB 安全機制](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/smb-security)、[AXFR RFC 5936](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936.html)。
五、如何證明防護真的有效？
這是整堂課最重要的部分。
假設公司訂定了以下規則：
「普通員工能讀取公告，但不能讀取財務資料；財務人員可以讀取財務資料。」
管理者應該測試不同身分，而不是只看一眼防火牆設定就宣布完成。

visual.caption: 圖 3｜模擬驗收：財務資料的存取權限
visual.description: 教學案例：以下皆為合成測試結果。切換身分，對照政策與觀察；固定假設是普通員工存在越權讀取，另外兩個案例符合各自受測操作的政策。沒有連線或實際登入，也不代表整台系統已通過驗收。

items.title: 外部訪客
items.body:
政策預期：不能讀公告或財務資料

實際觀察：公告與財務資料均拒絕讀取

受測操作符合政策

仍須核對核准員工的正常業務功能。

items.title: 普通員工
items.body:
政策預期：能讀公告，但不能讀財務資料

實際觀察：公告可讀，但也能開啟薪資清單

發現不符合政策的行為

發現越權讀取，應檢查檔案與群組的有效權限。

items.title: 財務人員
items.body:
政策預期：能讀公告及財務資料

實際觀察：公告與財務資料均可讀

受測操作符合政策

這只驗證讀取；修改與刪除權限須另依政策測試。

sourceBody.text: 這個測試其實包含兩種資安驗證方法：
Positive Test（允許案例）：原本應該能成功的事情，真的成功了嗎？
Negative Test（拒絕案例）：原本應該被拒絕的事情，真的被拒絕了嗎？
兩者缺一不可。
假設防火牆直接封鎖了整台檔案伺服器：

items: 訪客讀不到財務報表。
普通員工讀不到財務報表。
但財務人員也讀不到財務報表。

sourceBody.text: 這不是完整的防護驗收成功，因為正常業務功能也失效了。
六、為什麼「連線逾時」不代表安全？
假設你用一個網路測試工具，連線到某台伺服器，出現：
Connection timed out
請問這代表什麼？
它只能直接告訴你：在這次測試條件下，沒有在期限內得到預期回應。
可能的原因包括：

items: 防火牆刻意阻擋。
伺服器已經關機。
網路路由有問題。
服務沒有正常啟動。
測試目標或設定有誤。

sourceBody.text: 因此，資安報告不能直接寫「逾時代表防火牆保護成功」。
要證明防火牆真的阻擋，至少應尋找對應規則及實際流量紀錄，並確認來源、目的地、時間與測試內容一致。
這就是 CEH 必須建立的工程思維：不要把工具回傳的現象，直接當成原因。
七、日誌和告警，是監視器，不是門鎖
Log（事件日誌）像監視器錄影，Alert（告警）像警報器。
假設系統發現某個帳號在一分鐘內查詢了幾百個員工名稱。
系統可能會發出告警，但你不能直接宣布：「有人正在駭入！」
因為它也可能是合法的人事資料同步程式。
你需要進一步確認來源、使用者、查詢內容、時間、業務用途，以及過去是否有類似活動。
另外，就算日誌完整記下某人讀取機密資料，也不代表資料沒有外洩。
日誌負責留下證據，存取控制才負責限制行為。
八、整堂課整理成一套可用的方法
往後看到任何列舉防護問題，都可以依照這個順序思考。

items: 1. **先訂政策：**誰應該能從哪裡，對什麼資源做什麼？
2. **再做設定：**透過網路分段、防火牆、身分驗證、權限與加密機制落實政策。
3. **驗證允許：**正常使用者是否仍能完成工作？
4. **驗證拒絕：**不被授權的來源或帳號是否受到限制？
5. **取得證據：**設定、實際回應與日誌能否相互支持？
6. **修正再測：**未符合政策的地方是否確實改善？

sourceBody.text: 整個 M04 的知識可以這樣連起來：

items: 列舉技術教你發現系統對外揭露了什麼。
列舉防護教你決定哪些資訊可以揭露、哪些必須限制。
驗收測試教你用證據證明防護真的生效。

sourceBody.text: 換句話說，資安工程不是單純追求「查不到」，而是追求「在規定的條件下，得到正確的允許或拒絕結果」。
九、理解測驗：你來當資安工程師
假設你負責一間公司的網路安全，政策規定：

items: 訪客網路不得查詢內部設備管理資訊。
核准的監控主機必須能讀取設備運作狀態。

sourceBody.text: 測試發現：訪客連線逾時，但監控主機也無法取得設備狀態。目前沒有防火牆紀錄或服務日誌可供確認。
同事說：「兩邊都查不到，代表系統防護很成功！」
請你回答：

items: 1. 你同意同事的判斷嗎？為什麼？
2. 你認為目前哪些事情是已知事實，哪些還只是推測？
3. 你下一步會要求管理者提供什麼證據，才能判斷是否可以結案？

sourceBody.text: 請先寫下自己的答案，再展開參考解析核對。這裡不提交答案或記錄分數。

paragraphs: 不同意。核准監控主機無法取得狀態，已顯示正常功能未符合政策；訪客逾時也尚未證明是政策正確拒絕。
已知是兩種來源的本次測試都未取得預期資訊，且目前缺少可關聯日誌。防火牆阻擋、服務停止、路由故障或測試設定錯誤都仍是假設。
要求提供來源／目的地、測試時間與查詢內容、對應防火牆規則及命中紀錄、服務健康與授權設定、服務日誌。確認監控主機允許案例成功，訪客拒絕案例可歸因於政策，再保存修正後重測證據。

sourceBody.text: 這題真正要考的不是記憶防火牆指令，而是你能不能把「政策、觀察、原因與證據」四件事分清楚。

en.summary: Manage disclosure, data permissions and transport protection separately, using positive and negative tests to preserve legitimate service.

sourceBody.text: This lesson teaches a practical security principle: the right person should obtain only the information they need, under the right conditions.
Imagine a company server containing employee lists, financial records and device information. The policy has to support these needs:

items: Finance staff can use financial records normally.
Other employees can use information needed for their jobs but cannot read confidential files.
External strangers cannot freely probe internal systems.

sourceBody.text: Shutting down the entire server would prevent enumeration, but it would also prevent everyone from working. The goal is to preserve both security and availability.
1. Why can enumeration be risky?

Enumeration means asking a system, “What do you have here?” Imagine entering a company and asking reception: “What departments do you have? Who works here? Where is Finance? What computers and filing cabinets do you have?”

These questions do not directly steal a document. However, a stranger with a complete internal inventory can more easily identify targets for a later attack. Enumeration itself does not establish an intrusion: legitimate business also requires information queries.

visual.caption: Figure 1 | Three distinct outcomes for the same Finance folder
visual.description: These are parallel capabilities, without sequence arrows. Seeing a name does not grant reading; reading does not grant modification.

items.title: See the name
items.body: Know that Finance exists

items.title: Read the contents
items.body: Open financial statements

items.title: Modify the contents
items.body: Change financial statements

sourceBody.text: These three permissions are distinct. Seeing a folder name does not grant permission to read its files; permission to read does not grant permission to modify. Manage information disclosure, data reading and data modification separately.
2. Four checks for protecting a service
Think of a server as a building with security staff.

visual.caption: Figure 2 | A user wants to read server data
visual.description: Arrows indicate the order of these explanatory checks. Actual protocols need not execute in this sequence; transport protection can be established before login.

items.title: Check 1: Network reachability
items.body:
Does the firewall allow a connection to this service?

Like the building perimeter and entrance.

items.title: Check 2: Authentication
items.body:
Can the system establish who you are?

Like reception checking an employee ID.

items.title: Check 3: Authorization
items.body:
Even as an employee, which documents may you see and which operations may you perform?

Like checking whether you have a key to Finance.

items.title: Item 4: Encryption / Integrity
items.body:
Is data protected against observation or tampering in transit?

Like carrying files in a locked, tamper-evident briefcase.

sourceBody.text: Two common questions help distinguish the checks.
Question A: Why can I log in but still not read the data?
Authentication establishes identity; authorization grants permissions. You may be a confirmed employee without being a member of Finance, so you cannot read financial statements.
Question B: Does enabling HTTPS or TLS make the data safe?

TLS protects transmission and, when certificates are correctly validated, helps authenticate the server. If the service itself permits ordinary employees to read confidential information, TLS will securely deliver that information to someone who should not receive it.
3. What does least privilege mean?
Give a person only the permissions needed to complete their work, with no unnecessary extra permissions.
A cleaner may need access to corridors, meeting rooms and restrooms, but does not need the executive safe combination. The same principle applies to information systems.

headers: Capability that should not be granted

sourceBody.text: For example, an SNMP monitoring account needs router traffic and interface status, but does not need to change router configuration. Giving it the highest privileges may make the monitoring application work, yet a leaked account could then cause greater harm.
Ask both whether the function works and whether the account has more access than it needs.
4. How should the protocols from earlier lessons be protected?
The common approach across M04 is to limit unnecessary disclosure while retaining legitimate service.

rows: Keep normal name queries available; restrict AXFR zone transfers to approved parties
Control file reading, modification and deletion by identity
Control who can query which accounts and attributes
Restrict sources, security levels and readable or writable management objects
Control login, directory listing, downloads and uploads
Limit unnecessary user-verification and address-list discovery clues
Preserve time synchronization while restricting unnecessary management queries
Inventory dependencies, then restrict unnecessary entry points and disclosure

sourceBody.text: Two examples are useful for understanding CEH concepts.
Example 1: Is SNMPv3 automatically secure?

No. Suppose SNMP is upgraded to v3 with `authPriv`. With suitable configuration, messages receive authentication, integrity and encryption protection. But an account authorized to read all sensitive device information still has excessive access.

Use access controls such as VACM to restrict the management objects the account may actually read or modify. `authPriv` primarily addresses communication security; `read view / write view` primarily addresses operational permissions.
Example 2: Does SMB signing mean encryption?
No. Consider sending a document:

items: Signing resembles a verifiable seal that helps detect unauthorized modification of a message.
Encryption resembles a locked box that prevents an observer from reading the document in transit.
Access control decides whether the recipient is entitled to receive the document at all.

sourceBody.text: These mechanisms cannot replace one another.

Technical references: [SNMPv3 message security RFC 3414](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3414.html), [VACM RFC 3415](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3415.html), [Microsoft SMB security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/smb-security), and [AXFR RFC 5936](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936.html).
5. How can you demonstrate that protection works?

Suppose the policy says: “Ordinary employees may read announcements but not financial records; Finance staff may read financial records.” Test different identities rather than declaring success after inspecting a firewall setting.

visual.caption: Figure 3 | Simulated acceptance: access to financial data
visual.description: Teaching scenario: all results are synthetic. Select an identity to compare policy with observation. The fixed assumption is excessive access for the ordinary employee; the other two cases meet policy for their tested operations. No connections or real logins occur, and these cases do not establish whole-system acceptance.

items.title: External guest
items.body:
Expected policy: cannot read announcements or financial data

Observed: both reads denied

Tested operations match policy

Still check normal business functions for approved employees.

items.title: Ordinary employee
items.body:
Expected policy: can read announcements, but not financial data

Observed: announcements readable, but the salary list also opens

Behavior violates policy

Investigate effective file and group permissions for the excessive read access.

items.title: Finance staff
items.body:
Expected policy: can read announcements and financial data

Observed: both are readable

Tested operations match policy

This tests reading only; test modification and deletion separately against policy.

sourceBody.text: This exercise contains two security validation methods. A positive test asks whether an operation that should succeed actually succeeds. A negative test asks whether an operation that should be denied is actually denied. Both are necessary.
If a firewall blocks the entire file server:

items: Guests cannot read financial statements.
Ordinary employees cannot read financial statements.
Finance staff cannot read financial statements either.

sourceBody.text: This does not pass complete protection acceptance because legitimate business functionality also fails.
6. Why does a connection timeout not prove security?
Suppose a network test tool displays this result while connecting to a server:
Connection timed out
It directly establishes only that the expected response did not arrive within the time limit under those test conditions. Possible causes include:

items: A firewall deliberately blocked the traffic.
The server was powered off.
Network routing was faulty.
The service was not running correctly.
The test target or configuration was wrong.

sourceBody.text: A security report therefore cannot conclude “the timeout proves firewall protection worked.” To establish a firewall block, look for the matching rule and actual traffic records, and correlate the source, destination, time and test activity.
The engineering habit is to distinguish the phenomenon a tool reports from the cause that still needs evidence.
7. Logs and alerts are cameras, not locks

An event log resembles a surveillance recording; an alert resembles an alarm. Suppose an account queries hundreds of employee names within one minute. An alert may be generated, but that alone does not establish an intrusion: a legitimate HR synchronization application could generate the same activity.

Check the source, user, query contents, time, business purpose and historical activity before reaching a conclusion. Even a complete log of someone reading confidential data does not establish that disclosure was prevented. Logs retain evidence; access controls restrict actions.
8. A method you can apply to enumeration defenses
Use this sequence when evaluating a protection question:

items: 1. **Define policy:** who should be able to perform which operation, on which resource, from which source?
2. **Configure controls:** implement the policy through network segmentation, firewalls, authentication, permissions and encryption.
3. **Verify allowed operations:** can legitimate users still complete their work?
4. **Verify denied operations:** are unauthorized sources or accounts restricted?
5. **Collect evidence:** do configuration, actual responses and logs support one another?
6. **Correct and retest:** have policy mismatches actually been resolved?

sourceBody.text: The M04 lessons connect in this way:

items: Enumeration techniques reveal what information a system exposes.
Enumeration countermeasures define which information may be disclosed and which must be restricted.
Acceptance tests use evidence to establish whether controls take effect.

sourceBody.text: Security engineering seeks the correct allow or deny result under the specified conditions, while preserving legitimate work.
9. Understanding check: act as the security engineer
You manage a company network with this policy:

items: The guest network must not query internal device management information.
Approved monitoring hosts must be able to read device status.

sourceBody.text: Testing shows that guest connections time out, but monitoring hosts also cannot obtain device status. No firewall records or service logs are currently available to explain the results.
A colleague says, “Neither side can query anything, so protection is very successful!” Answer these questions:

items: 1. Do you agree with that judgment? Why?
2. Which facts are known, and which explanations remain hypotheses?
3. What evidence would you request from the administrator before deciding whether to close the issue?

sourceBody.text: Write your own answer first, then expand the reference explanation. This page does not submit answers or record scores.

paragraphs: Disagree. The approved monitoring host cannot obtain status, so legitimate functionality already fails policy. A guest timeout also does not establish a correct policy denial.

Known facts: neither source obtained the expected information in these tests, and correlated logs are unavailable. Firewall blocking, service failure, routing failure and incorrect test configuration remain hypotheses.

Request source and destination, test time and query, matching firewall rules and hit records, service health and authorization settings, and service logs. Verify successful approved monitoring and a guest denial attributable to policy, then retain evidence of the corrected retest.

sourceBody.text: The question assesses whether you can distinguish policy, observation, cause and evidence, rather than memorize a firewall command.
